newsitem.title: ISRAEL: PLO police rally to aid stone-throwing youth.
newsitem.headline: PLO police rally to aid stone-throwing youth.

text.p: "Come on, shoot, show them what can be done," one youth jeered at a Palestinian policeman who was frantically shouting into his walkie-talkie and trying to calm demonstrators.

Youths raining stones and bottles on Israeli troops near the West Bank town of Ramallah initially cursed Palestinian police for not defending them when Israeli bullets on Wednesday sent scores of wounded demonstrators to hospital.
But jeers turned to cheers when Palestinian paramilitary forces took up positions behind shrubs and houses to return fire at Israeli soldiers.
"When we saw there was a massacre and the Israeli soldiers were entering our area, we had to respond," one officer told Reuters after the clashes had subsided.

"Go back and give the chance to your national forces to do their national duty," blared loudspeakers as crowds crouching on streets littered with stones and bullet casings began shouting old revolutionary songs extolling armed struggle against Israel.
"They are coming to the war and we will follow them," one youth shouted.
Israeli soldiers shot dead three Palestinian policemen and one civilian in the clashes. The Israeli army said seven of its soldiers were lightly wounded.
When two truckloads of Palestinian police bearing Uzi submachine guns rolled onto the scene, crowds began chanting "Allahu Akbar (God is Great)".
Police sheltered behind walls and cars to return fire at Israeli troops, some of whom had taken position on hills and rooftops.
Witnesses said Palestinian police struggled to clear the area of civilian demonstrators, sometimes pushing and shoving youths away from the front line to prevent further clashes.
Civilians, who dropped to the street in waves when gunshots rang overhead, whistled to alert Palestinian police to Israeli positions.

"The Israelis don't realise that the Palestinian people are emotionally worked up out of frustration that the peace process has gone nowhere," one Palestinian security official told Reuters on the scene.
"If they want war, you can see the Palestinians are ready for it," he said.
